sources.note: Sect. 2 Phonology (pp. 70-73: consonants, vowels, minimal pairs, syllable structure (C)V(C)(V)(C), morphophonemics) contains NO statement of where stress falls. The only mention is indirect, sect. 2.5 p. 73: 'Vowels in a final syllable may be dropped, or centralised, if the word has more than one syllable. The vowel in the unstressed syllable becomes schwa [ə]. e.g. 'apun completive particle > ['apm] ~ ['apəm]' — one stress-marked example (initial = penultimate in a disyllable), no rule.

sources.note: Comparative; Musom appears only in correspondence tables and etymologies (data source listed as Hooley 1971, p. 407). No Musom or Markham stress statement; the one stress remark in the Huon Gulf chapter (p. 157) is about Proto Hote/Buang unstressed-vowel deletion.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii + 236 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-C115
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sect. 4.2.10 Musom (pp. 56-57, Table 4.11) is a phoneme inventory with five segmental notes only; nothing on stress. The volume's only stress remarks concern Duwet (note 11, p. 57: last vowel of a vowel sequence becomes [ə] in unstressed position) and a comparative remark on Watut final-consonant loss 'through stress rules' (p. 88). Tone is stated to be phonemic only in Labu (p. 63 note 7), Yabem and Bukawa (p. 3). The earlier scan's 'not found online' classification was wrong: the PL DOI resolves to an open CC BY-SA PDF (and the text was already held by the project).

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne Carol. 1988. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea: a history of the Austronesian languages of the Markham and Ramu Valleys, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. xxiii + 446 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/1885/133945
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full-text search of the thesis text layer: the same three stress mentions as C-115 (Duwet unstressed vowel sequences; Watut 'stress rules'; Duwet *e reflex 'iə in unstressed syllables'); no statement on Musom stress.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1985-88. Markham languages fieldwork, 1985-88 (audio recordings of informant interviews, 15 languages incl. Musom). ANU Open Research dataset.
sources.note: Primary audio for Musom (1985 recordings); the only route to an instrumental or auditory determination of stress placement, since no text source states it.
